title: Take over a stale user host lock under a claim, so two runs never both hold it
summary: When two `ia host claude --user` runs found the same stale lock, `<IA home>/claude/.lock`, at the same moment, both could take it over and go on to change the marketplace at once. @inventarch/distribution now removes a stale lock only under a claim, an exclusive `.lock.<inode>.claim` directory beside it, and only after finding again that the lock path still names the file it judged, so two runs on one host never both remove it and a lock another run created in the meantime is left in place. A claim older than 10 seconds is abandoned and removed, and a run that acquires the lock sweeps abandoned claims. On Windows the exclusive create now waits up to 250 milliseconds for a lock name another run is still removing, instead of failing with a raw EPERM. A create refused for permissions (on Windows, once that wait passes with nothing at the name; elsewhere at once, where a raw EPERM or EACCES was thrown before) refuses IA-DIST-INPUT-INVALID, naming the directory. Earlier CLIs do not claim, so a run of an earlier release sharing the IA home can still remove a lock without one.
